title: Capacity, breadth and commitment, measured
intro: Each of the three analogs is a number produced by a specific procedure, run against a specific control. This level gives the procedures: what was fitted, what the control was matched on, which population the comparison ran against, and where the paper marks its own measurement as approximate.

chapters.title: Counting what is in there
chapters.body:
Occupancy is a fitting problem, solved once at every position and layer. [[sparse-decomposition]] looks for a non-negative combination of $K$ [[j-lens-vector]]s that best reconstructs the [[residual-stream]] at that point. The [[j-space]] is defined by exactly this operation. [[eq-jspace-cones]] writes it as the union, over every size-$K$ subset of lens vectors, of the cone of their non-negative combinations, and [[eq-jspace-distance]] gives an activation's distance to that set as the smallest reconstruction error over those subsets.

A fit of this kind cannot say for itself when to stop. Adding one more vector always lowers the reconstruction error, so error alone would keep counting upward.

The control supplies the stopping rule. The same fit is run with a same-size set of random directions, and [[j-space-occupancy]] is the value of $K$ at which the improvement from one more lens vector drops below the improvement from one more random direction.

That count is near zero through the first third of the layers. It rises to a plateau of about 25 across the [[workspace-layers]] in the median case, and the paper notes the value varies across contexts. The onset lines up with a band that had already been located by four other statistics.

The variance figure is a second use of the same control. With $K$ held at the median occupancy, the fraction of activation variance the top $K$ lens vectors explain in excess of a random set of the same size never exceeds 10% at the five workspace layers tested ([[fig-30]]).

The count also does work backwards. [[sparsity-level-k]] is fixed by hand rather than derived, and the paper concedes the choice is somewhat arbitrary; occupancy is the measurement that justifies keeping it at or below 25.

A [[sparse-autoencoder]] run gives the same answer from a different dictionary: only a small share of features have decoder directions aligned with the J-space, and the unaligned ones are dominated by low-level syntactic and bookkeeping features.

chapters.title: Six words, and what displaces them
chapters.body:
The [[word-list-experiment]] fixes a threshold before it counts anything. A list word counts as present at a given comma if its best [[j-lens-readout]] rank over the workspace band falls in the top 25, and the paper varies that threshold to show the qualitative result does not turn on it.

The experiment began from an observation rather than a hypothesis. After the model has read one word of an animal list, shark, the readout already holds whale, fish, swimming, submarine and ocean, almost none of which appear in the list. After eight animals it is dominated by animal words, read or unread.

So the lists were split in two. On lists of unrelated words, about six of the words read so far are present at any comma, and the number stays flat as the list runs on; older entries drop out. On single-category lists, close to the whole eighty-word family is present within a few items, including the words the model has not reached yet ([[fig-31]]).

The paper reads the second case down rather than up. A category held as the collection of vectors that constitute it is not the same as eighty entries recalled at once.

[[category-displacement]] is the timing result. Eight animals followed by eight colors leaves the readout dominated by colors after a single color word, and lists built from four twenty-word blocks repeat the pattern. Within a block, individual words persist long after being read.

One further deflation: [[single-layer-capacity]] repeats the count at layer 79 alone and finds one or two unrelated concepts rather than six ([[fig-72]]). Part of what the pooled figure measures is storage spread across depth, which is one place the analogy to [[working-memory]] does not carry over cleanly.

[[workspace-competition]] adds the load case. Two held concepts share tokens at the shuffled control rate, 0.46 against 0.53, while a held concept and a running arithmetic problem almost never share a token, 0.09 against 0.29 ([[fig-73]]).

chapters.title: Gain, and what it is measured against
chapters.body:
[[mlp-gain]] is computed on the weights, with no forward pass behind it. For a unit direction $v$ at layer $\ell$, it is the output norm of the MLP block at layer $\ell+1$ applied to $v$, divided by the median output norm that block gives to isotropic random directions. Random directions therefore score 1 by construction, and every number is a multiple of chance.

The choice of comparison population is what gives the result its force. The lens vectors are set against the output-weight directions of the previous layer's MLP neurons, two thousand unit directions drawn per population. Those neuron directions are the model's own units of computation, so a lens vector amplified ten times more than they are is not merely beating noise ([[fig-32]]).

A second population grades the same claim continuously. Sparse-autoencoder decoder directions are split into six equal strata by [[lens-kurtosis]], the sharpness of a direction's lens readout, used here as a graded measure of J-space alignment. Gain orders monotonically across the strata, and the bottom half sits at baseline.

One stratum overshoots. In the early workspace layers the top-kurtosis features are amplified more than the lens vectors themselves, and the paper takes that as a limit on its own instrument: the lens is confined to single vocabulary tokens, so those features may approximate the model's workspace directions more closely than the lens does.

The metric is flagged as approximate in the paper's own footnote. Real gain depends on what else the activation carries, and this measurement holds nothing else.

Two appendix analyses take the same question to individual neurons. Within the band, the share of neurons whose strongest weight match is a lens vector rises from roughly 15% to 60-65% ([[fig-77]]), and connection strength above a random-direction threshold shows the same ordering ([[fig-78]]). Read-side connections peak early in the band and write-side connections late. This is what makes [[j-space-broadcast]] a [[weights-only-population-comparison]] rather than a behavioral one.

chapters.title: The heads, and what zeroing them costs
chapters.body:
Relay quality is two numbers, both taken from a head's [[ov-circuit]], the combined value-then-output map that says what an [[attention-head]] writes about whatever it attends to. Gain is the mean of $\|W_{OV}\,v\|$ over the population, normalized on random directions as before.

[[label-preservation]] asks whether the head copies a direction or scrambles it into the others. For each $v_i$ it ranks $\cos(W_{OV}v_i, v_i)$ among the cross terms $\cos(W_{OV}v_i, v_j)$ and reports the mean reciprocal rank, contrasted against the same statistic on random directions so that a head copying everything indiscriminately scores zero.

[[broadcast-heads]] are then the top 1% of workspace-layer heads scored by the worse of their two ranks. A head must do both things to qualify.

Six populations were run through the same selection. One of them is the lens vectors under a fixed random orthogonal rotation, which preserves their spectrum and their pairwise geometry while destroying their identity; it is the control that separates being J-space directions from merely being that shape. The heads selected for the lens vectors separate cleanly from every comparison population on both metrics ([[fig-33]]), and they concentrate in the first half of the band, where the J-space's effective rank is lowest and one OV map can carry more of it.

The ablation zeroes those heads at every position, against equal-sized layer-matched random heads over five seeds. Recall@25 is the fraction of the unablated run's top-25 lens tokens still in the top 25 afterwards, and at the worst mid-workspace layers it falls to 0.67 against the control's 0.86, while the top-1 next token changes at 5% of positions against 2% ([[fig-34]]).

The behavioral checks are where the dissociation bites. Reporting of an injected thought falls from 0.54 to 0.09 while the control leaves it intact ([[fig-7]]), and on the [[experiential-reports]] prompts the head ablation reproduces roughly a third of the drop caused by full [[j-space-ablation]].

chapters.title: Committing to one reading
chapters.body:
The [[embedding-mixture-experiment]] manufactures ambiguity at the input rather than looking for it. A concept token's input embedding is replaced by the mixture $(1-\alpha)\,e_B + \alpha\,e_A$ inside an ordinary carrier sentence, sixteen pairs of single-token country names across forty sentences, with $\alpha$ swept from 0 to 1 and the residual stream recorded at that position at every layer.

The first readout deliberately avoids the lens. [[projection-share]] places the activation on the line joining the same trial's pure-$B$ activation to its pure-$A$ activation, at the same position and layer, so the ends of the sweep sit at 0 and 1 by construction. Early layers track $\alpha$ smoothly; from about layer 38 the value sits near one end or the other and switches at a threshold ([[fig-29]]).

[[transition-width]] puts a number on the switch: the change in $\alpha$ needed to move the share from 10% to 90%. It falls steeply over roughly layers 21 to 42. Measured separately for the component along the two concepts' lens directions and for the complement with the top sixteen lens vectors projected out, the J-space component is consistently narrower and reaches its floor earlier ([[fig-70]]).

An average sitting mid-way admits two readings. Every trial might be genuinely undecided, or trials might each commit and split evenly.

[[bimodal-commitment]] separates them. At the most ambiguous $\alpha$, the per-trial shares pile up near 0 and near 1 ([[fig-71]]). At early layers both components sit near 0.5; by mid-depth the J-space component is clearly bimodal while its complement still has mass in the middle.

What this licenses is narrow. The sharpening is an analog of [[ignition]] in timing and shape, measured on artificial blended embeddings, and it corroborates the [[layer-bands]] boundary without using the lens to do so.
